key_insight: Training-only LLM filtering of potentially unreliable EEG sleep-stage labels improved TinySleepNet classification without adding inference-time complexity.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support lightweight, wearable sleep-stage monitoring, though clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Train TinySleepNet on original labels and flag low-confidence epochs.
Use LLaMA 3.1 to assess flagged epochs using EEG spectral features, sequence context, and AASM scoring guidelines.
Remove epochs judged suspicious and retrain TinySleepNet.
evidence_signal: On Sleep-EDF Expanded with 20-fold cross-validation, accuracy rose from 81.8% to 84.6% and macro F1 from 75.6% to 77.4%, with notable REM detection gains.
watch_item: Low-confidence epochs may include valid, difficult examples; the abstract does not report independent expert validation of the LLM's filtering decisions.
paper_title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
